tech.cardLabelNote: “{label}” on the card comes from <mono>{source}</mono> and does not follow the name; the name is the technology’s own (shown in the research screen’s tooltip and research slots).
tech.days: Research takes about {days} days (base {base} days × {cost}, before the ahead-of-time penalty and research bonuses)
tech.otherBlock: This one is given by another block of the history file (a DLC condition block or a start date’s block), not by the starting set_technology list, so it cannot be switched off here.
tech.startNote: Written into {tag}’s history file as set_technology; the follow-up technologies it opens or closes change once the research tree is read again.
tech.newNote: The new technology goes on this page and this line, and can be researched once this one is (this one gets a path to it); its categories are this one’s. Add the equipment and modifiers it gives, and its picture, in the technology workbench.
tech.confirmDelete: Delete this technology? Links pointing to it are removed too.

problem.nameInvalid: The name cannot contain quotes or line breaks
problem.idTaken: The ID {id} is taken; choose another name
problem.xInvalid: The horizontal position must be a whole number from 0 to 20
problem.costInvalid: The research cost must be above 0

specialProject.gameShownNote: The name and description on the card and the project page are localisation text, not the workbench’s name and description above; the workbench has no breakthrough points needed to start.
specialProject.description: Description (the text on the project page)
specialProject.available: When it can start (available; FROM is the country)
specialProject.conditionsNote: Conditions are written as game script; leave one empty to remove it.
specialProject.problemWorkbench: The name and description cannot be empty; breakthrough points are whole numbers from 0 to 100
specialProject.problem: The name and description cannot be empty; breakthrough points are whole numbers from 0 to 100; a discount covers 1 to 100 designs at 0 to 100%
specialProject.noteWorkbench: The name is saved as the card’s localisation text, the description as the project page’s; the breakthrough points go into this workbench row and are written back as they are on export.
specialProject.note: Saving takes the whole file holding this special project into your project and changes only this block; one made in the special projects workbench changes its row instead. The name is saved as the card’s localisation text, the description as the project page’s. The discount changes the add_design_template_bonus of the same name in the special project’s output (in every branch that has it).

insignia.logoUploaded: Uploaded the picture of intelligence agency insignia “{name}”
insignia.newLabel: New insignia for {tag} with this picture
insignia.names: Names (one a line; the game picks one at random; localisation keys work too)
insignia.availablePlaceholder: Leave empty = every country can choose it
insignia.default: Which countries use it by default (default)
insignia.conditionsNote: Conditions are written as game script, e.g. original_tag = GER.
insignia.problem: At least one name is needed, and names cannot contain quotes, braces or #
insignia.note: Saving takes the whole file holding this insignia into the project and changes only this block; an insignia made in the intelligence agency workbench changes its row instead.

upgrade.agencyGone: This intelligence agency is no longer in the project
upgrade.upgradeGone: This upgrade is no longer in this intelligence agency
upgrade.workbenchLacks: The workbench has no name, factories used while under way or start condition; change them here:
upgrade.factories: Civilian factories used while under way
upgrade.levels: Effects of each level (one block a level, as game script)
upgrade.problemLevels: The name cannot be empty, factories are 0 to 100, and every level needs its effects
upgrade.problem: The name cannot be empty, and factories are 0 to 100
upgrade.noteLevels: Saving takes the whole file holding this upgrade into the project and changes only this block; an upgrade of an agency made in the intelligence agency workbench changes that row instead. The name is saved as the localisation text of the upgrade’s id.
upgrade.note: Saving changes this upgrade in this intelligence agency workbench row; the name is saved as the localisation text of the upgrade’s id.

mio.takenIn: Took {count} military-industrial organizations from {file} into the project
mio.gone: This military-industrial organization is no longer in the project
mio.fromGame: This military-industrial organization comes from the game files and is not in the project yet. To change it, first take the whole file declaring it into the project (the other organizations in that file come along); the export writes it back under the same name, replacing the game’s file.
mio.takeIn: Take into the project and edit
mio.overridden: A trait inherited from the template that this organization’s override_trait has changed: each item the override writes replaces the inherited one as a whole block.
mio.inherited: A trait inherited from the template: saving writes it as this organization’s override_trait with only the items changed; bonuses replace the inherited ones as whole blocks.
mio.placeRelative: Column {x}, row {y} on the tree; the position counts from the {anchor} cell.

scientist.extrasNote: The characters workbench lacks the two items below: the skill in each specialization (the editor above changes only the first specialization and its level), and traits not listed above (another specialization’s, or others from the game or the mod).
scientist.levels: Skill level in each specialization (0 = none)
scientist.locked: The editor above has unsaved changes: save it first, then change this (both write the same row)
scientist.note: This changes this person’s row in the project (the same row as in the characters workbench), which goes into the game on export.
